listen.script: Hi, I'm Omar. On Saturday, my family went to the desert. We left home very early, at six o'clock. My father drove the car, and my sister and I played games. We arrived at nine o'clock and had breakfast under a big tree.

listen.script: Noura wanted to buy a present for her mother. First she thought about flowers, but her mother has lots of flowers in the garden. In the end, she bought a blue scarf, because blue is her mother's favourite colour.
listen.q: What did Noura buy for her mother?

read.passage: My name is Sara, and I live in Jeddah with my parents and two brothers. Every Friday, we visit my grandmother. She lives near the sea, so after lunch we usually walk on the beach. But last Friday was different. It was too hot outside, so we stayed in the house. My grandmother taught me how to make date cookies. They were delicious! Next week, I'm going to make them for my friends at school.

qs.q: Why didn't Sara's family walk on the beach last Friday?
What is Sara going to do next week?

speak.prompt: Tell me about a special day with your family, like Eid or a family trip. Where did you go, and what did you do?
speak.expect: At A2 (GSE 30-32), the learner can give a short, simple description of a past event in a few linked sentences, using basic connectors such as 'and', 'then', 'but' and 'because'. They mostly use the past simple correctly, including common irregular verbs (went, ate, saw, had), though errors may appear. They use everyday vocabulary for family, food, places and feelings (e.g. 'We went to my uncle's house. We ate kabsa. I was very happy because I got new clothes.'). They may add a simple opinion or reason. Expect pauses, some reformulation and a limited range of structures, but the message stays clear and understandable without much help from the examiner. They should be able to answer one simple follow-up question, such as 'Who did you see?'
